previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with hypotension and chest pain following a dialysis session. Initial concerns included sepsis due to his dialysis line, but blood cultures showed no growth, and antibiotics were discontinued after 48 hours. The hypotension was attributed to fluid removal during dialysis, worsened by diarrhea and poor oral intake. His chest pain resolved in the ED, and serial troponins showed only a minor elevation, consistent with baseline. Diarrhea resolved, and stool studies were negative for pathogens. He remained stable on the medical floor, completed scheduled dialysis, and was discharged home after three days with instructions to follow up with nephrology and cardiology, monitor weight, and start Nephrocaps.

EXCHANGE OF TUNNELED HEMODIALYSIS CATHETER.

INDICATION:  ___ man with tunneled hemodialysis catheter, with
coag-negative staph infection.

OPERATORS:  Drs. ___ (fellow), ___ (resident) and ___.
___ (attending physician).  Dr. ___ was present throughout the procedure.

CONTRAST:  None.

SEDATION:  Moderate sedation with divided doses of intravenous ___ mcg
fentanyl and 2 mg Versed over 51 minutes, during which patient's hemodynamic
status was continuously monitored by a trained radiology nurse.

PROCEDURE AND FINDINGS:  Consent was obtained after explaining the benefits,
risks, and alternatives.  Patient was placed supine on the imaging table in
the interventional suite.  Timeout was performed as per ___ protocol.

Initial scout fluoroscopic image demonstrated left jugular venous tunneled
hemodialysis catheter tip in the right atrium.  Under aseptic conditions,
about 5 mL of blood was aspirated from both ports to remove the indwelling
heparin.  0.035 stiff Glidewires were placed via both ports and advanced into
the IVC.  Blunt dissection was performed along the tunnel to release the
adhesion around the catheter and cuff.  The catheter was then removed by
gentle traction over the wires.  A new 15.5 ___ 32 cm tip-to-cuff catheter
was placed over the wires. Catheter tip was confirmed under fluoroscopy to be
in the right atrium.  Wires were removed.  Ports were aspirated and flushed. 
Catheter was secured by 0 silk sutures.  Site was appropriately dressed. 
Patient tolerated the procedure well and no post-procedure complications were
seen.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated replacement of left jugular venous tunneled
hemodialysis catheter with a new 15.5 ___ 32 cm (tip-to-cuff) catheter.  It
is ready for use.  Tip of the previous catheter was sent for laboratory
analysis.
